title: Calendar grid has no grid semantics or row-based navigation for screen reader / keyboard users
where: index.html:3938 (`<div className="grid">`) and the day-cell buttons built at 3915-3936
detail: Each day is an independent `<button>` with a rich aria-label (dt.toDateString() + shift/take-home/OT/note info, lines 3916-3922) — that part is done well. But the container has no `role="grid"`/`role="row"`/`role="gridcell"` and there is no roving-tabindex or arrow-key handling; the weekday header row is `aria-hidden="true"` (line 3952) with no equivalent exposed elsewhere. Every day in the visible month(s) is one flat Tab stop in a single sequential order.
failure: A keyboard or screen-reader user who wants to check the take-home for a date three weeks out must Tab through every single day between today and then one at a time — there is no 'next week' / row-jump the way a native `role="grid"` (arrow keys) would give them, and nothing announces that this region is even a calendar grid rather than an arbitrary list of buttons.
fix: Wrap each week row in `role="row"`, mark cells `role="gridcell"` inside a `role="grid"` container (or, more simply, add a `role="grid"`/roving-tabindex layer per WAI-ARIA APG's grid pattern) so assistive tech can navigate by week/row instead of one cell at a time.
